source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into Windows. 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on the client 5. Using the following command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>mc.dimminfo() >>>ei.injectMemError(socket, channel, dimm, sub_channel,rank=0, errType="ce") >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Memory slot 1~N (Intel correctable ECC on Memory slot 1~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'corrected|CE_|CE |EDAC|memory.error'; echo __correctable_ECC_on_Memory_slot_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

test_case.test_name: Memory slot 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject one correctable ECC event into every in-scope populated memory slot, verify the OS/BMC/UEFI evidence attributes it to that exact slot, and confirm the platform remains healthy without asserting front-panel or DIMM lightpath fault indicators.
required_package: Supported Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash and `ce` injection semantics
Approved slot/rank coverage matrix and bounded injection count
Authoritative Windows/BMC/UEFI correctable-event fields and indicator applicability
test_case.test_command: An FAE/operator maps inventory and `mc.dimminfo()` tuples to physical slots, enables the approved BIOS controls, performs one `errType=ce` injection per authorized tuple, resumes the Windows SUT, verifies normal service, collects slot-specific RAS records and physical no-light evidence, then restores settings. Rank/sub-channel coverage is defined before the run rather than assumed from rank 0.
test_case.expected_result: 1. System should work normally 2. BMC error log should record which slot has DIMM correctable error 3. Front Panel fault Light will not Light if there is one 4. Corresponding DIMM lightpath will not light if there is one 5. uEFI SEL Log should record which slot has DIMM correctable error if there is one

safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, console and FAE approval
Preserve baseline records rather than clearing them
Cross-check every tuple with physical slot before one injection
Stop for wrong-slot attribution, unbounded error count, unexpected lamp, crash or loss of console
No automatic retry; restore BIOS and validate memory health before another target
expected_evidence: Package hash, full `mc.dimminfo()` and approved tuple-to-slot/rank matrix
Per-slot injection transcript and authoritative Windows corrected-ECC evidence
BMC and applicable UEFI SEL naming the same physical slot
Timestamped front-panel/DIMM-lightpath off evidence, normal health, BIOS restoration and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The hybrid workflow requires package and user/FAE confirmation; it is not agent-direct. Unavailable topology or indicator evidence blocks execution, not the static review or DUT verdict.
